sources.title: AGA Clinical Practice Guideline on the Role of Biomarkers for the Management of Ulcerative Colitis
sources.authors: Singh S, Ananthakrishnan AN, Nguyen NH, Cohen BL, Velayos FS, Weiss JM, Sultan S, Siddique SM, Adler J, Chachu KA; AGA Clinical Guidelines Committee
sources.studyDesign: GRADE-based guideline; systematic evidence synthesis + Evidence-to-Decision framework; 7 conditional recommendations
sources.licence: Not stated in retrieved metadata (Europe PMC license field null; isOpenAccess=N). Treat as All Rights Reserved, AGA / Elsevier.
sources.studyPopulation: Adults with established ulcerative colitis, in symptomatic remission or with active symptoms
sources.ucSpecificSampleSize: Not applicable (guideline synthesising multiple studies); underlying diagnostic-accuracy evidence base not enumerated in retrieved abstract
sources.interventionOrExposure: Non-invasive biomarker-based monitoring (fecal calprotectin, fecal lactoferrin, serum CRP), alone or with symptoms
sources.outcomes: Detection of endoscopic/active inflammation; avoidance of routine endoscopy; treatment-decision guidance

regionalApplicability.assessment: US professional-society guideline. Concepts transfer to Canada, but fecal calprotectin assays are not interchangeable, cut-off calibration and lab availability/reimbursement differ, so thresholds need local validation.

sources.limitations: All 7 recommendations are conditional (generally low / very-low certainty evidence). Retrieved as structured abstract only; full recommendation tables, thresholds rationale, and evidence profiles were not accessed. Biomarker thresholds are decision aids, not diagnostic cut-offs for an individual.

sources.title: STRIDE-II: An Update on the Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (STRIDE) Initiative of the International Organization for the Study of IBD (IOIBD): Determining Therapeutic Goals for Treat-to-Target strategies in IBD
sources.authors: Turner D, Ricciuto A, Lewis A, D'Amico F, Dhaliwal J, Griffiths AM, Bettenworth D, Sandborn WJ, Sands BE, Reinisch W, Scholmerich J, Bemelman W, Danese S, Mary JY, Rubin D, Colombel JF, Peyrin-Biroulet L, Dotan I, Abreu MT, Dignass A; IOIBD
sources.publishingOrganisation: International Organization for the Study of Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IOIBD)
sources.studyDesign: Systematic literature review (11,278 records screened, 435 included) + iterative Delphi consensus of 89 IOIBD members; consensus threshold >=75%; 15 recommendations drafted, 13 endorsed
sources.licence: Not stated in retrieved metadata (Europe PMC license field null; isOpenAccess=N). Treat as All Rights Reserved, IOIBD / Elsevier.
sources.copyrightHolder: AGA Institute / Elsevier Inc. (published on behalf of IOIBD)
sources.studyPopulation: Adults and children with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease)
sources.ucSpecificSampleSize: Not applicable (consensus initiative). UC-specific element: histological healing addressed as a measure of remission depth, not a formal target.
sources.interventionOrExposure: Treat-to-target management strategy; defined short-term, intermediate and long-term treatment targets
sources.comparator: Symptom-only / non-target-based management (historical comparator, not formally tested here)
sources.outcomes: Consensus-defined therapeutic targets: clinical response/remission, CRP/ESR and fecal calprotectin normalisation, endoscopic healing, absence of disability, quality of life, normal growth in children

regionalApplicability.assessment: International consensus (IOIBD); Canadian and US IBD experts among authors. The document explicitly states targets should be adapted to local resources, so implementation (test access, monitoring intervals) still needs regional tailoring.

sources.limitations: Consensus-based; many targets rest on low-certainty evidence. IBD-general (UC + Crohn's) - not a UC-only document; UC-specific monitoring intervals and biomarker cut-offs are not defined in the retrieved abstract. Retrieved as structured abstract only.
